Revised assessment incorporating July 2019 SLOOS:
- The FOMC’s 25 bp cut and early end to balance-sheet runoff remain cautiously accommodative, aiming to support growth amid below-target inflation.
- SLOOS evidence points to tighter credit conditions on the business side: banks tightened standards and other terms for C&I loans and for construction/land development (CRE), with weaker demand reported for construction/land development. These findings align with softer business investment cited by the FOMC.
- Consumer credit looks more mixed-to-stable: standards and demand for other consumer loans were largely unchanged, with some willingness to lend; government-backed loan demand stronger but standards mixed. This provides only a modest offset to business-side tightening.
- Net effect: SLOOS tilts conditions more cautious than the initial read, reinforcing the Fed’s risk-management rationale and tempering the overall positivity of the statement.
